## Target
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py` — **793 LOC** on origin/main against the 800-LOC hard cap
(7 lines of headroom).

## The concern boundary: BLOCKING checks vs NEVER-BLOCKING checks

The module's own docstring already states the invariant this split cuts along: "The only sound,
unambiguous blockers are therefore **P1, P4 (description), P5 (cycle), P8, P10, and P11**.
Everything else is advisory or coverage-only."

That documented boundary is also a real seam in the CALL GRAPH. The four never-blocking checks —
**P2 resolution**, **P3 package-existence**, **P6 AC/DD quality**, **P7 destructive-sniff** — have
ZERO call edges, inbound or outbound, to any other function that stays in `det_floor.py`:

- `p2_resolution` and `p3_package_existence` call only `rebar.grounding.refute_absence` (lazily
  imported) plus their own private extraction regexes `_FILE_REF_RE` / `_PKG_REF_RE`.
- `p6_ac_quality` is a pure aggregation hub over the ALREADY-EXTRACTED advisory-lint siblings:
  `det_operator_attested.ac_item_lines`, `det_clarity.vague_hits_in_line`,
  `det_lint._verify_command_strings` / `_lint_verify_command`,
  `det_operator_attested.operator_evidence_issues`,
  `det_measurement_provenance.provenance_issues`, `det_citation.unbacked_citations`. Moving it puts
  the hub in a module beside its spokes instead of in the floor's core.
- `p7_destructive` calls nothing; it owns `_DESTRUCTIVE_RE` / `_SAFEGUARD_RE` outright.

The checks that STAY are the ones that are actually connected: `p1_readiness_shape` and
`p4_oversize` both call `_count_ac_items`; `p1_readiness_shape` calls `_clarity_score`; `p4_oversize`
calls `_description_limit`; `p8_reviewability` calls `est_tokens`; `p5_task_dag` calls
`det_lint._find_cycle` / `_file_interference`. Cutting between those two sets removes 246 lines
without severing a single existing call edge.

## Established precedent this follows
`det_clarity.py` (P10/P11) and `det_lint.py` (P9 + pure helpers) were extracted from this same
module on this same seam and re-exported from `det_floor.py`. This change is the third application
of a pattern the package already uses, including its cycle-avoidance contract:
`from __future__ import annotations` + `TYPE_CHECKING` for the `DetResult` / `PlanContext`
annotations and a lazy `from .det_floor import DetResult` inside each function body, so there is no
runtime import back into `det_floor`.

## What moves
New module `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_advisory.py` receives these definitions verbatim:
`_FILE_REF_RE`, `p2_resolution`, `_PKG_REF_RE`, `p3_package_existence`, `p6_ac_quality`,
`_DESTRUCTIVE_RE`, `_SAFEGUARD_RE`, `p7_destructive`.

Function bodies alone are not self-contained: `p6_ac_quality` calls `vague_hits_in_line(ln)`,
`_verify_command_strings(ctx)` and `_lint_verify_command(cmd)` as BARE names, bound today by
`det_floor.py`'s module-level import block. So `det_advisory.py` declares its own module-level
imports, mirroring those bindings:

```python
from .det_clarity import vague_hits_in_line
from .det_lint import _lint_verify_command, _verify_command_strings
```

plus `import re`, `import logging` if needed, `from __future__ import annotations`, and
`from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any` with `DetResult` / `PlanContext` imported under
`TYPE_CHECKING`. `p6_ac_quality`'s other dependencies (`det_citation`,
`det_measurement_provenance`, `det_operator_attested`, `rebar._reads`) are already IN-BODY lazy
imports, so they travel with the body untouched. `p2_resolution` / `p3_package_existence` likewise
carry their in-body `from rebar import grounding`. Each moved function gains one added line, the
lazy `from .det_floor import DetResult`, exactly as `det_clarity.p10_verification_presence` and
`det_lint.p9_file_impact_coverage` already do.

Symmetrically, `det_floor.py` DROPS the three imports whose only consumer was `p6_ac_quality`
(`vague_hits_in_line` from `.det_clarity`; `_lint_verify_command` and `_verify_command_strings`
from `.det_lint`), while keeping `_find_cycle` / `_file_interference` (used by the retained
`p5_task_dag`) and the `decomposition_state_block` / `veto_undecomposed_g5` re-exports that
`pass1.py` reaches through `det_floor`.

`det_floor.py` remains the ENTRY MODULE and dispatcher: it keeps `DetResult`, `PlanContext`,
`est_tokens`, the `DET_CHECKS` tuple, `run_det_floor`, and the finding/coverage aggregation
(`det_finding_has_subject`, `det_blocking_findings`, `det_advisory_findings`, `det_coverage`), and
re-exports all four moved checks so every existing import point and every `det_floor.<check>`
attribute access keeps resolving unchanged.

## Why the retained half is the half that stays
Three tests bind to the `det_floor` MODULE OBJECT and would silently stop testing anything if their
target moved:
- `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py` monkeypatches `det_floor.DET_CHECKS`.
- `tests/unit/test_af77_config_fault.py` monkeypatches `det_floor.run_det_floor`.
- `tests/unit/test_plan_review_prerequisites.py`, `..._heldout.py` monkeypatch
  `sizing.det_floor.est_tokens`.

All three targets are in the RETAINED half. `_clarity_score`, `_count_ac_items` and
`_description_limit` are imported by name from `det_floor` by lockstep/migration tests and also
stay. No moved symbol is monkeypatched anywhere; every reference to a moved symbol is either a call
through the re-export or a `from ... det_floor import` that the re-export satisfies.

## Sizes
`det_floor.py` 793 -> ~550 (approx 250 lines / 31% headroom); `det_advisory.py` ~300. Both inside the
200-500 target band; neither under 100.

## Registry sweep (path-keyed artifacts)
Checked before implementing, updated in the same change if they fire:
- `.github/complexity-baseline.json` — grep confirms **zero** entries keyed to
  `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py`, so no moved symbol carries a ceiling and the ratchet
  cannot report `new>0`. Re-verified with `scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`.
- `tests/scripts/test_llm_seam_clean_heldout.py` `_OWNED_FILES` / `_MARKER_BUDGET` — lists
  `llm/plan_review/det_floor.py`. No config read moves (`_description_limit`, the module's only
  `compose_config` call, stays), so the new module must report zero config-ownership findings and
  zero `# read-via:` markers; verified by running `scripts/check_config_ownership.py`.
- `.github/module-size-limit.txt` — NOT touched. The gate and `tests/module_size_support.py` are
  path-agnostic (`rglob`), so the new file needs no registration.
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` and `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py` name `det_floor.py` as the
  layer-1 home; docstring/prose repointed to name the new sibling. Prose only, no assertions.

## Verification
- `pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review.py tests/unit/test_det_floor_clarity.py
  tests/unit/test_det_floor_operator_attested.py tests/unit/test_g5_decomp_det.py
  tests/unit/test_plan_review_prerequisites.py tests/unit/test_af77_config_fault.py
  tests/unit/test_ticket_description_limit.py tests/unit/test_a8e5_det_hygiene_edge.py
  tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py tests/scripts/test_llm_seam_clean_heldout.py
  tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_criteria_heading_collapse.py` — all pass with NO test file edited
  to accommodate the move.
- `make lint`.
- `make typecheck`.
- `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`.
- `test $(wc -l < <file>) -le 720` per resulting file.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `test $(wc -l < src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py) -le 720` exits 0.
- [ ] `test $(wc -l < src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_advisory.py) -ge 100` exits 0.
- [ ] `python -c "from rebar.llm.plan_review.det_advisory import p2_resolution, p3_package_existence, p6_ac_quality, p7_destructive"` exits 0.
- [ ] `python -c "from rebar.llm.plan_review.det_floor import p2_resolution, p3_package_existence, p6_ac_quality, p7_destructive"` exits 0, proving the re-export preserves the old import point.
- [ ] `python -c "import rebar.llm.plan_review.det_advisory as m; assert m.vague_hits_in_line and m._lint_verify_command and m._verify_command_strings"` exits 0, proving `p6_ac_quality`'s bare-name dependencies are bound at module level in the new home.
- [ ] `git diff --stat origin/main -- tests/` reports no changed test file other than a prose-only docstring repoint.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review.py tests/unit/test_det_floor_clarity.py tests/unit/test_det_floor_operator_attested.py tests/unit/test_g5_decomp_det.py tests/unit/test_plan_review_prerequisites.py tests/unit/test_af77_config_fault.py tests/unit/test_ticket_description_limit.py tests/unit/test_a8e5_det_hygiene_edge.py tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py tests/scripts/test_llm_seam_clean_heldout.py tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_criteria_heading_collapse.py` exits 0.
- [ ] `git diff --exit-code origin/main -- .github/module-size-limit.txt` exits 0.
- [ ] `make lint` exits 0.
- [ ] `make typecheck` exits 0.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` exits 0 with `new=0 increased=0`.
- [ ] The commit message names the blocking-vs-never-blocking concern boundary as the seam, stating the call-graph evidence.
